title: Decide one project with two solves

blocks.text: A transit agency's fleet-renewal MILP chooses which depots to rebuild, and maximizes the value of the plan. The board wants to know about one depot in particular: must it be in the plan? The analyst runs the model twice, once with that depot's variable fixed to 1 (forced in) and once fixed to 0 (forced out). Each run returns its incumbent and its best bound, or nothing at all when the run proved that no plan exists with the depot fixed that way.
Write `fund_or_skip(forced_in, forced_out)` in `fund_or_skip.py`. Each argument is a pair `(incumbent, bound)` for a maximization, or `None` for a run that proved no plan exists. Return:

items: `"fund"` when every plan without the depot is worse than a plan with it: the forced-in incumbent is strictly greater than the forced-out bound, or the forced-out run has no plan.
`"skip"` when every plan with the depot is worse than a plan without it: the forced-out incumbent is strictly greater than the forced-in bound, or the forced-in run has no plan.
`"undecided"` otherwise: the two brackets overlap or touch, and only tighter runs can tell.

blocks.text: The two runs never both return `None`.

cases.says: when the forced-in incumbent beats the forced-out bound, fund
when the forced-out incumbent beats the forced-in bound, skip
when the brackets overlap the answer is undecided, whichever incumbent is higher
an incumbent equal to the other run's bound beats nothing, so the answer is undecided
when no plan includes the project, skip
when no plan leaves the project out, fund

origin.section: Plans Within the Gap Can Pick Different Projects
